premature

/pree-muh-CHOOR/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Premature means happening or done before the proper time — too soon, when things are not yet ready or right.

The fans' premature celebration turned to silence when the other team scored in the final seconds.

Example

The startup's premature launch of its app left thousands of users battling crashes the developers had not yet fixed.

The launch didn't just happen early — it happened before the app was ready, before the proper time. That 'before it should have' judgment is what premature adds beyond plain 'early.'

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

untimely: Untimely means happening at a bad or wrong time — an untimely death, an untimely interruption — and often too soon. It grieves over the timing. Premature is more clinical and specific: the thing happened before its proper time, before conditions were ready. Untimely mourns when it happened; premature pinpoints that it happened too soon.

hasty: Hasty means done with too much speed and too little preparation — a hasty apology, a hasty exit. It faults how rushed the doing was. Premature faults the calendar instead: however carefully something was done, it came before the proper time. A launch can be meticulous in execution and still premature.

ill-timed: Ill-timed means landing at an unlucky or awkward moment — an ill-timed joke can come too soon, too late, or just in the wrong setting. Premature is narrower: the fault is always the same one, arriving before the proper time. Every premature announcement is ill-timed, but an ill-timed remark may simply have hit the wrong moment.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

timely: happening at exactly the right moment

overdue: coming later than it should have

Where it sits · how much blame the act draws — early → premature → rash

early vs. premature: Early is weaker — it neutrally means before the scheduled time, and can even be a good thing; premature adds that the thing came before it properly should have.

rash vs. premature: Rash is stronger — it condemns the careless judgment behind an act, while premature only faults its timing.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pre-

Prefix — pre-: before, in advance (Latin prae-)

Root — mature

Root — mature: ripe, fully developed (Latin maturus)

Put it together

Put it together: Pre- ('before') + maturus ('ripe') builds 'ripe before its time.' Something premature arrives before it has properly ripened — like fruit picked green.

Use the root in a new word: maturation

Use the root in a new word: maturation: The cheese spends eighteen months of maturation in the cellar below the shop.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / slightly formal

Premature pairs naturally with nouns like celebration, conclusion, announcement, and judgment ('it's premature to say'). Unlike plain 'early,' it almost always implies the timing was a mistake — something happened before it properly should have. In medicine, it describes babies born before full term.
